# Live - Refactoring avec Terraform

## Accroche

Pitch : refactorer une infra de prod fait peur parce que le state suit le code à la trace. Les blocs `moved` rendent le refactoring déclaratif, versionné, relu en revue. On monte du rename simple au split vers un module d'équipe plateforme, et chaque étape se termine sur un plan « no changes ».

**Titre event** : `❯ live tech_ · Refactoring avec Terraform`

**🔬 Description event - v1 générée (2026-08-25, rejetée : « avec la preuve à chaque étape », vocabulaire interdit → voix v1.14, corpus instance 31)**

**✅ Description event - v2 validée Baptiste (2026-08-25, à publier dans l'event)** :

> Live technique, démos dans le repo public.
> Jeudi 27 août, 13h. LinkedIn + Twitch.
>
> Renommer une ressource, sortir un bloc vers le module de l'équipe plateforme : le code bouge, et le state ? Sans précaution, terraform plan répond destroy puis create.
>
> On refactore en direct avec les blocs moved : du rename simple jusqu'au split d'un root module vers un sous-module. À chaque étape, la même sortie : un plan « no changes ».
>
> Au menu aussi : ce qui se passe dans le state, les bonnes pratiques producteur et consommateur de modules, et les limites du mécanisme.

## Corps

### Conducteur - Refactoring avec Terraform (live S35, jeu. 2026-08-27, 13h)

Sujet tranché en décision directe (ADR-009, cf. [[2026-08-03 Live - Harness agentique d'un repo OSS]] §Suivi post-live), annoncé dans le retex S34. Démo = lab public `examples/terraform-state-refactoring` sur [bgauduch/terraform-examples](https://github.com/bgauduch/terraform-examples). Découplage : le repo ne référence jamais ce live.

Public : praticiens IaC et équipes plateforme qui font vivre des modules et des infra de longue durée. Héros : le bloc `moved`. Scène : terminal + micro-deck.

#### Idée-force

Le state est une table d'association blocs ⇔ ressources. `terraform state mv` l'édite à la main, un env à la fois, sans relecture. `moved` l'édite en code : versionné, relu, propagé à tous les envs par le même commit.

Fil rouge : **le refactoring se lit au plan** - la destination est toujours la même sortie, « no changes ».

#### Structure (conducteur timé en cours de production, jalons Phase 2)

Fil prio (~35 min de cœur) :

| Bloc | Support | Objectif |
|---|---|---|
| OPEN | cam | accueil, format, invite chat, partage d'écran confirmé |
| WHY (S0) | slide | la peur du state ; micro-historique : state mv impératif → moved v1.1 |
| WHAT (S1) | slide | state = table d'association ; moved = édition déclarative de la table |
| HOW-1 · rename | terminal | démo 1 : mise en conformité de nommage, state pull avant/après, plan « no changes » |
| HOW-1bis · sous le capot | terminal | deep-dive : manipulation des références, delta vs terraform state mv, propagation multi-env |
| HOW-2 · split | terminal | démo 2 : migration vers le module de l'équipe plateforme pour rentrer en conformité |
| LIMITES (S2) | slide | même type requis · pas cross-state (relais = removed + import, cf. live S25) · rétention child/root · force-replacement |
| CLOSE | slide récap + CTA | matrice de choix par cas d'usage (moved / state mv / removed+import), repo |

Bonus numérotés (joués si avance au jalon mi-live, dans l'ordre) :
1. `for_each` impacté par le split.
2. Bump v2 du sous-module : `moved.tf` + `migration.md` livrés par le module ; v3 enchaînée = cascade de moved (saut de majors).
3. `removed` (`destroy = false`) sur la ressource intruse + ré-adoption par bloc `import`.
4. Dogfooding : refactorer un exemple existant du repo, puis `git restore` (décision au pré-vol).

Beats verrouillés, coupes et phrases de sortie : figés en Phase 2 avec les mesures du lab.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /Users/bgauduch/Obsidian Vault/.claude/skills/add-editorial-slides

# Add Editorial Slides

Generate a branded HTML slide deck (interactive, browser-first) for a piece. Distinct artifact class from PNG visuals (§5.0): multi-slide, responsive 16:9, delivered as-is (opened in the browser). The skeleton fixes the frame + slide-type components; Claude assembles **semantic slides**, never absolute coordinates. A **legibility gate by per-slide inspection** + brand-review lock the result. Content FR.

## SSoT - read at runtime, never restate

| Concern | Source |
|---|---|
| Slides format spec (composition rules, slide-types catalogue, layout, navigation) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/03-Design-system.md` §5.7 |
| Format registry (dims, naming, home) | `03-Design-system.md` §5.0 |
| Color tokens + WCAG ratios | `03-Design-system.md` §1.1 / §1.2 |
| Executable skeleton (frame + slide-type classes + slot markers + nav) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/skeletons/slides.html` |
| HTML->PNG renderer (QA, supports `?slide=N`) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs` |
| Voice (positive phrasing §2.7, Golden Circle arc §2.9) | `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` |
| Asset naming, piece link, lint gate | `02-Areas/Éditorial/CLAUDE.md` |

Reverse-engineering from an existing deck is forbidden (BGA CLAUDE.md Asset production contract). The skeleton is the only structural base.

## Input

`--piece <path>` (required). Source = the piece body: `## Accroche` (hook), `## Corps` (Why → How → What), key bullets, tables.
`--scope intro|full` (optional, default `intro`): `intro` = short deck (~5 slides: title, context/Why, key cases or points, one synthesis table, transition); `full` = cover the conductor.
`--out <path>` (optional): override output; default `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/slides-<subject>.html`.

## Workflow

### 1. Read the piece + outline the deck
- Read the piece. Extract: the hook (`## Accroche`), the Why → How → What spine, key bullets, any tables (reuse **verbatim** as `table` slides).
- Build a slide list: pick a slide-type per idea via the **§5.7 archetype heuristic** (content→format table, read at runtime). Catalogue, archetypes and heuristic live in §5.7 only - never restate the mapping here. `intro` scope: keep ~5 slides. Positive phrasing (§2.7), one idea per line, Golden Circle arc (§2.9).
- Lead slide = `title` (piece H1 + a key fragment in `<span class="hl">` + a framing `sub`). Close = `flow` or a `title` transition ("place à la suite").

### 2. Clone the skeleton
- Copy `Brand/skeletons/slides.html` → `<out>` (default `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/slides-<subject>.html`, `<subject>` kebab-case from the piece). Collision → suffix `-2` and warn.

### 3. Fill the slides region (semantic HTML, never coordinates)
- Replace content between `<!-- slot:slides:start -->` / `<!-- slot:slides:end -->` (markers only, never line numbers). Missing/orphan marker → explicit abort, no fallback.
- One `<section class="slide">` per slide, first one `active`. Use the skeleton's component classes per slide-type (§5.7). **Add `.slide-logo` (wordmark top-right) on every slide except `title`** (the cover carries the big wordmark) - the skeleton reference slides show the markup. Reuse the piece's tables as-is for `table` slides; emphasise the key cell with `class="em"` and the last row is auto-highlighted.
- Compose HTML that lays itself out (no fixed heights/positions; text must wrap). Keep each slide concise to fit the frame - the engine does not shrink the font; split a dense slide in two rather than overflow.

### 4. Legibility gate (per slide, blocking)
- For each slide N: `node "02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs" "<out>?slide=N" /tmp/<subject>-<N>.png 1280 720`, then **Read the PNG**. Check: no overlap, no text outside its frame or truncated, legible hierarchy (kicker < h1/h2), the slide fits. Any anomaly → fix the HTML (concision, split), re-render. The PNG is authoritative, not the HTML.

### 5. Brand-review gate
- Run the `brand-review` skill: `--visual <out> --visual-png <representative slide PNG> --text <piece>`.
- Pre-check (blocking, ADR-001 - the procedure lives in `check-colors.mjs`, never restated here): run it on **every slide**, `node "02-Areas/BGA Consulting/Brand/_pipeline/check-colors.mjs" <out>?slide=N` for N in 1..total. A slide-1 sample is NOT a gate: a defect that lives in one slide-type ships undetected. Measured on the skeleton itself (2026-08-10): `?slide=1` green while 2 of 18 slides failed V4.
- Verdict ≠ PRÊT (incl. V9 legibility) → fix, re-render, re-review. Steps 4+5: max 3 loops, then surface the residual.

### 6. Wire the piece (idempotent)
- In `## Notes production`, add/refresh one line pointing to the deck: ``Deck de slides : `assets/slides-<subject>.html` (ouvrir au navigateur ; flèches / clic, `f` plein écran, `l` mode pointeur).`` Re-run with the same deck = no-op. Slides are a live-support artifact, not a `## Visuels` PNG entry - keep them out of the `## Visuels` brief.
- Run `python3 02-Areas/Éditorial/scripts/lint-editorial.py --file <piece> --apply`; report residual violations.

### 7. Return
- Deck path. Slide count + slide-types used. Legibility gate: OK | fixed (n loops). Brand-review verdict (+ manual residuals). Piece wiring: applied | already present.

## Rules
- **Read §5.7 Règles de composition before outlining**, not just the slide-type catalogue. They decide *which* slide exists; the catalogue only decides what it is made of. They are read at runtime, never restated here - a rule written there applies to the next generation without depending on the agent's memory.
- **Two blocking slides**, checked before returning: a destination teaser and a récap + CTA. A live deck without them is non-conforming (retex S30: both planned, neither prepared, neither played).
- Skeleton = structural SSoT. No reverse-engineering of existing decks; changing the frame or slide-types = amend §5.7 + the skeleton first.
- **Layout delegated to CSS**: never absolute positioning, never hand-computed coordinates. Compose semantic slides with the skeleton classes.
- Colors = closed whitelists: hex §1.1, translucent derivatives §1.1bis. Missing value → STOP, amend the design-system. Alpha never on ink.
- Text on light background respects WCAG §1.2. The amber accent token is decorative only (bars, arrows), never text (§7).
- Interactive HTML is the deliverable; the PNG is QA-only (no delivery PNG). An illegible slide is never delivered, even if tokens/WCAG pass.

# CLAUDE.md - BGA Consulting

Rules for `02-Areas/BGA Consulting/`.

## Area map

Business area = brand + ops. Folder map (Brand detailed below; ops folders here):

| Folder / note | Scope | Entry point |
|---|---|---|
| `Brand/` | Design truth, editorial render pipelines | `Brand/README.md` |
| `Juridique/` | Statuts, objet social, transformation, RC Pro | `Objet social EURL - dossier de conformité` (objet social SSoT) |
| `Comptabilité/` | Accounting, fiscal + social arbitrages | `2026-04-14 Point comptable...` |
| `Fournisseurs/` | Per-vendor records | one note per vendor |
| `Stratégie de gestion.md` | Management vision + EURL calendar | top-level note |

Note naming: dated events (meetings, points) `YYYY-MM-DD Topic`; durable analyses/SSoT keep a stable name; per-workstream status notes allowed (e.g. EURL transformation suivi).

## Brand SSoT

`Brand/README.md` is the index. Never re-decide specs - read the doc.

| Topic | Doc |
|---|---|
| Method / phases | `Brand/00-Plan-construction-charte.md` |
| Positioning, targets, anti-positions | `Brand/01-Brief.md` |
| Visual direction (indigo + amber) | `Brand/02-Moodboards.md` |
| Colors, typo, tokens, grid, WCAG | `Brand/03-Design-system.md` |
| Logo specs / usage | `Brand/04-Logo.md` |
| Voice, lexicon, mail signature | `Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` |
| Roadmap, per-support specs | `Brand/06-Roadmap-declinaisons.md` |
| Copy observations feeding the voice (LLM draft vs validated version, typed deltas) | `Brand/Corpus copy - généré vs validé.md` |

Identifiers (SIREN, mail, Calendly, EURL): auto-memory `reference_bga_identifiers.md`.

## Branding scope

Branding owns design truth and brand decisions, not tooling or content.

- Owns: tokens, typo, grid, WCAG, format specs, logo, voice, positioning. SSoT = `Brand/`.
- Out of scope: rendering pipelines/scripts (→ Asset pipelines), editorial idea→piece workflow + per-channel publication tactics (→ `02-Areas/Éditorial/`), post/article content.
- Design docs state what the design *is*, never how it is rendered. Tooling paths live in Asset pipelines / scripts, never in `Brand/03-Design-system.md`.

## Asset production contract

Before producing or editing any brand asset (visual, banner, slide, doc, CV):

1. Read the SSoT first: tokens `Brand/03-Design-system.md` §1.1, translucent derivatives §1.1bis, WCAG §1.2, format spec (§5.0 visual-format registry, roadmap per-support). Never reverse-engineer from an existing asset - assets drift, SSoT never (mirror of the note-template rule, vault root CLAUDE.md).
2. Colors + format = closed whitelists. Hex ∈ §1.1, `rgba()` ∈ §1.1bis. A value or format absent from the design-system → STOP, amend the design-system first, then produce. Never improvise an opacity either (ADR-014).
3. **Gate, run it, never eyeball it**: `node Brand/_pipeline/check-colors.mjs <html[?query]> [--pdf]` (exit 1 = blocking). V3 = the two whitelists + alpha never on ink + zero alpha on a PDF delivery path. V4 = WCAG §1.2 measured on the **rendered composite**, since a `porteur` derivative changes the real backdrop. Decorative text is exempted by `data-decor`, any other exemption is declared inline (`brand-exempt: <reason>`). Touching the checker or §1.1/§1.1bis/§1.2 → `node Brand/_pipeline/test-check-colors.mjs` green first.
4. The amber accent token is decorative only (filets, bars, arrows, series glyphs), never text (§7). Its value lives in §1.1, nowhere else.
5. On completion: bump the touched phase-doc version + journal in `Brand/README.md`; re-validate WCAG if tokens changed.

## Editorial

All BGA text follows `Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md`:
- Positive phrasing default (principle 2.7). Exceptions: Do/Don't, anti-positions, blocking rules.
- Participatory "on" for shared live/demo action (principle 2.10, default in `live`); "je" reserved for authorship asides. Distinct from the banned corporate "nous" (2.8).
- Anti-positions: no hype, no dark-tech-bro, no corporate-consulting, no jargon.
- Brand adjectives: posé, précis, chaleureux, exigeant, pédagogique, épuré.
- **Ad-hoc copy gate**: WHEN producing BGA copy outside a skill, Claude MUST read `Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md` at runtime and pass `brand-review` before delivery (miss: corpus instance 21).
- **After any copy validation**: log the delta in `Brand/Corpus copy - généré vs validé.md`.
	- 3 occurrences of one pattern → arbitrate, then amend the voice doc.

Editorial schema/workflow: `02-Areas/Éditorial/CLAUDE.md`. Tone + piliers SSoT: `Brand/01-Brief.md` §16 + `Brand/05-Tone-of-voice.md`.

## Brand folder layout (closed convention)

`Brand/` = SSoT prose at root (`README.md` + `00-06*.md`) + asset families + shared tooling. Every asset family follows the same contract; new supports clone it, never invent a new shape.

- **Observation journal** at `Brand/` root, next to the numbered phases: a log that feeds a phase doc, growing per published piece (`Corpus copy - généré vs validé.md`).
	- Same frontmatter shape as phase docs; version bumped on each ruling; listed in `Brand/README.md`.
	- Adding one = a convention change: journal entry in `Brand/README.md` required.
- **Asset family** `Brand/<family>/`: `sources/` (editable origin) + `exports/` (generated PNG/derived). Families hold **reusable identity assets only** (rendered once, reused across many pieces): `logo/`, `moodboards/`, `photos/`, `banner/` (profile banner), `stream/` (OBS overlays). **Per-piece content renders** are NOT a Brand family - they live in `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/` via `add-editorial-visual` (ADR-006). Discriminator: reused across pieces → Brand family; produced for one specific piece/event → `Éditorial/assets/`. Visual format registry: design-system §5.0.
- **`skeletons/`**: executable forms of design-system specs. Editorial visual formats: skeleton = `skeletons/<format>.html`, specs in design-system §5.0 registry. Email signature: `signature-email.html` (tone-of-voice §5.2).
- **Asset versioning** (asset families): `vN` = validated major, the only one consumers reference. `vN.x` = working iterations toward the next major. Never a new major per attempt.
	- **Only the current major is gated.** Superseded majors are history: readable, never maintained, out of `check-colors.mjs` and out of any re-render. Running a gate over them is expected to fail and means nothing (ADR-014). Corollary: a doctrine change never back-propagates to them.
- **Shipped is frozen** (same principle, all asset classes): once the deliverable is out, the source that produced it stops being gated. Discriminator = **is the source itself the deliverable?** A `slides` deck is delivered as HTML (§5.0), so it stays live and gated. A `carousel` ships a PDF, an `event-banner` or `square` ships a PNG: once published, frozen. A utility page that is never published (teleprompter, preview chrome) declares `brand-exempt-file:` with its reason. Applies to `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/` too.
	- On validation: promote the retained `vN.x` to `v(N+1)`, then prune every `vN.x`.
	- Pruning also requires lessons traced (phase doc + README journal) and the workflow updated so the defect cannot recur.
	- Prune last, never first. Git stays the archive.
- **`_pipeline/`**: shared HTML→PNG node toolbox (Playwright). Holds `render-html.mjs` (generic), `render-banner.mjs` (banner wrapper), `package*.json`, `node_modules/` (gitignored). The only renderers that share Playwright live here; `logo/` (system Chrome) and `photos/` (own python `.venv` + `build.py`) keep their engine inline because the runtime differs.

## Asset pipelines (reuse, don't reimplement)

- **Logo (SVG→PNG)**: `Brand/logo/render.sh <svg> <out.png> <width> [bg]` (Chrome headless + Manrope). Sources `Brand/logo/sources/`, exports `Brand/logo/exports/`. Batch: `Brand/logo/render-all.sh`.
- **LinkedIn banner (HTML→PNG, gated)**: `node Brand/_pipeline/render-banner.mjs v<N>` reads `banner/sources/banner-v<N>.html` → `banner/exports/banner-bga-v<N>-<date>.png` + generated `qa-overlay-v<N>-<date>.png`; log in `Brand/README.md`.
	- Geometry SSoT `Brand/banner/safe-zones.json`, read at runtime. Model + rationale: `Brand/06` §2.1.
	- Render is **blocking**: `check-banner-safezones.mjs` measures `[data-critical]`/`[data-important]`, a violation writes no file. Annotate criticality in the source; never eyeball safe zones.
	- Touching the checker or the spec → `node Brand/_pipeline/test-check-banner-safezones.mjs` green first.
	- Keep Playwright (uses `document.fonts.ready`); don't switch to raw Chrome.
- **Generic HTML→PNG (shared)**: `node Brand/_pipeline/render-html.mjs <html> <out.png> <width> <height> [transparent]` (arg-driven, @2x, waits `document.fonts.ready`; optional `transparent` → alpha PNG for OBS overlays). Reuses the `_pipeline/` Playwright install. Used for any fixed-size HTML asset (editorial square visual, OG, stream overlay, ...).
- **Editorial visuals (HTML→PNG)**: skill `add-editorial-visual`, format dispatch per design-system §5.0 registry (skeleton `skeletons/<format>.html`, dims from §5.0). HTML/CSS auto-layout mandatory (no hand-placed coordinates). Render via `_pipeline/render-html.mjs`; output → `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/<format>-<sujet>.{html,png}` (per-piece content, ADR-006).
- **Editorial slides (HTML deck)**: skill `add-editorial-slides`, skeleton `Brand/skeletons/slides.html` (design-system §5.7). Composed from the piece, HTML/CSS auto-layout. Legibility gate per slide (`?slide=N` rendered via `render-html.mjs`) + brand-review; output → `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/slides-<sujet>.html` (per-piece, ADR-006). Interactive HTML delivered as-is, no delivery PNG.
- **Editorial carousel (HTML→PDF)**: LinkedIn document post (design-system §5.8, ADR-007), skeleton `Brand/skeletons/carousel.html`. N pages portrait 4:5 (1080x1350), HTML/CSS auto-layout. Legibility gate per page (`?page=N` via `render-html.mjs` 1080 1350) + brand-review; **delivery PDF** `node Brand/_pipeline/render-pdf.mjs <html> <out.pdf> 1080px 1350px` → output `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/carousel-<sujet>.{html,pdf}` (per-piece). Per-page PNG transient (QA only), not persisted. Skill `add-editorial-carousel` (skeleton + per-page gate + brand-review + PDF delivery + wire into the piece `## Visuels` + lint); hand-craft from the skeleton stays possible.
- **OBS stream scene (HTML→PNG)**: skeleton `Brand/skeletons/stream-scene.html` (executable form of design-system §5.5) → copy to `Brand/stream/sources/scene-<name>[-perso]-v<N>.html`, activate one recipe, fill slots → `render-html.mjs <html> <out.png> 1920 1080 transparent` (live-* scenes; starting-soon renders opaque, no 5th arg). Exports `Brand/stream/exports/scene-<name>-v<N>-YYYY-MM-DD.png`.
- **New support**: apply the discriminator first. A **reusable identity asset** → new family `Brand/<support>/{sources,exports}` (banner is the template). A **per-piece content render** → skeleton in `Brand/skeletons/` + instance in `02-Areas/Éditorial/assets/` via `add-editorial-visual` (ADR-006), never a Brand family. Render web supports via `_pipeline/render-html.mjs`. Slide decks = `skeletons/slides.html` + skill `add-editorial-slides` (HTML interactif, design-system §5.7), rendu live au navigateur ; Keynote en option pour decks non-techniques.

## Mission output contracts

- **Audit**: findings, risk assessment, prioritized recommendations.
- **Build**: production-ready, documented, handoff-ready.
- **Run**: reliability, observability, incident response, minimize toil.
- **Support**: unblock fast and clear.
- **Training**: pedagogical, progressive, reusable.

## Governance

- Phase doc change: bump version + journal entry in `Brand/README.md`.
- Color token change: re-validate WCAG (`Brand/03-Design-system.md` §1).
- **SSoT reference propagation**: consumers reference design-system sections by number (§1.1 tokens, §1.1bis translucent derivatives, §1.2 WCAG, §5.0 visual-format registry, §5.4/5.5/5.6 visual specs, §5.7 slides, §5.8 carousel) - markdown refs do not auto-track. Any renumber/restructure/value change of these sections MUST update consumers in the same commit. Consumers: skeletons `Brand/skeletons/*.html`, **`Brand/_pipeline/check-colors.mjs` (parses §1.1/§1.1bis/§1.2 at runtime, so a table shape change breaks it - its test suite is the tripwire)**, skills `add-editorial-visual` + `add-editorial-slides` + `add-editorial-carousel` + `brand-review`, editorial `02-Areas/Éditorial/CLAUDE.md`, roadmap §2.8. Inverse: a skill citing a section is responsible for the path being resolvable (full path in its SSoT table).
- **One home per check procedure** (ADR-001, re-asserted by ADR-014): `brand-review` owns it, the create skills call the checker. A skill that restates a check is a regression, not a convenience.
- Old `Charte graphique.md` archived - don't revive.

# Session Handoff

Make the session resumable from a cold context: the rich trace lands in the project's **tracking file** (it owns priorities), nothing is lost, the next session starts from one short prompt.

Honors: `feedback_tracking_files_always_uptodate`, `feedback_para_archivage_extract_forward_looking`, `feedback_scope_discipline_endorsed_actions`, `feedback_ssot_no_restate_in_skills`, `feedback_git_mv_then_edit_restage`. Lesson routing per global `CLAUDE.md` (memory vs `tasks/lessons.md`).

## 1. Scan the session
`git status --short` + `git log --oneline` (this session's commits) + `git diff --stat`. List built / changed / decided / discovered. Separate MY changes from unrelated working-tree edits (parallel sessions) - never sweep those in.

## 2. Locate the tracking file (SSoT for priorities)
Project living doc: backlog / `tasks/todo.md` / project-main / MoC / PLAN. Glob the working dir + common names. Ambiguous or none → ask which (or to create one). Match its language for everything below. An Area doctrine is a durable living doc, not a session tracker: it may receive the §4 reconcile (backlog items with triggers, dated journal) but NEVER the §7 resume region.

## 3. Verify state (oracle)
Find + run the project's check command (tests / validator / linter / build / typecheck). Record the exact command + result. Red → fix in scope or flag it prominently in the prompt (don't hand off a broken tree silently).

## 4. Reconcile the tracking file (the dump)
Edit it to carry:
- One-line **status/progress** (themes done/total, % if used).
- **Done** items → mark resolved + trace (commit / ADR / file).
- **Decisions** taken + alternatives discarded + revisit-trigger.
- **Every leftover / deferred / debt** → a **live, trackable item** under the right priority, each annotated with **value** and **trigger** ("do only if X", "revisit when Y / at volume ×5"). Track **debt** as its own category. Never leave future work living only in a journal entry, a resolved item's prose, or a to-be-deleted note.
- A dated **journal entry**: done / decisions / deviations from plan / frictions / reste. Past-tense only - no "à venir"/"next" inside a journal line (forward-looking → live item; a stale "upcoming" line contradicts newer entries).

## 5. Route lessons
Corrections + frictions this session → formulate a rule that prevents recurrence. Cross-project → auto-memory (`feedback_*`); repo-specific → `tasks/lessons.md`. Iterate an existing rule, don't stack a duplicate.

## 6. Traceability gate (before any deletion)
Enumerate each decision / discovery / leftover / blocker and map each to a durable home (tracking item / ADR / subtree CLAUDE.md / schema / code docstring / commit / memory). Anything living **only in chat or a disposable note** → persist first. Only then may a disposable scratch/plan note be `git rm`'d - surface + confirm. Re-stage after any `git mv`+Edit.

## 7. Persist + emit the resume prompt → tracking file (disposable) + `pbcopy` + print
Write the lean prompt into the tracking file in a **disposable anchored region**, just under the H1/frontmatter so a cold start sees it first - **only where the note's own structure declares that section**. Vault: templates are a closed whitelist (`99-Templates/`, resolved by `type:`), and only `type: project` `role: main` declares it. Template silent, or note type absent from the map → **no write at all**: `pbcopy` + print + an explicit warning ("prompt en presse-papier uniquement, pas de section Reprise dans le template de cette note"). NEVER create the section where the template lacks it, and never in an Area doctrine or a Resource. Read the region before writing: orphan or duplicated anchors → abort, no fallback write (vault: hybrid-editing contract). Heading in the tracking file's language (vault note → FR), e.g.:
```
## 🔄 Reprise (jetable - régénéré à chaque handoff, pas d'historique)
<!-- skill:handoff:resume:start -->
_MAJ <YYYY-MM-DD>_

…prompt…
<!-- skill:handoff:resume:end -->
```
**Overwrite** the region every run (replace, never append - only the latest matters). Re-read after writing: stamp = today, exactly one anchor pair. A stamp older than today means the overwrite missed - fail loudly, do not proceed to §8. Also `pbcopy` + print (clipboard is volatile; the note is the persistence). Content, short + paste-ready:
- 1-line project + state ("X done, committed").
- **Reload list (cold-start warm-up)** = the explicit set of links to open before acting, drawn from what actually proved useful this session: files touched (§1), SSoT/pattern docs consulted, reference notes / sub-projects, relevant memories by name. **Tracking file first** (SSoT for priorities + journal). Render each as a real link - wikilink `[[Note]]` / `[[Note#Section]]` for a note, backtick path for a non-note file (per `feedback_obsidian_reference_links`) - plus a 3-5 word *why*. This is the materialized context-rewarm: keep it to the 5-8 that matter, not an index of the repo.
- **Oracle command** (run to confirm green) + last known result.
- **Blockers / prerequisites** (env, MCP, auth, login) - or "none".
- **Next step** = the single top unresolved item: one line + pointer to its tracking item (e.g. "détail : P1"). Never restate the item's content (attachments, sub-steps) - it drifts between handoffs; the item is the only home. No meta-commentary about the rule in the note itself.
- Key conventions/gotchas + "start in plan mode, confirm scope before acting".

## 8. Checkpoint commit (restore point BEFORE trim)
Commit the non-destructive work so far - reconcile (§4) + resume region (§7) + in-scope files - per project convention (this vault: on `main`, dedicated commit, no branch). This is the **restore point** before the lossy compaction: if §9 misfires, `git checkout <this commit> -- <tracking file>`.

## 9. Compaction pass (synthetic, no loss, no dup) - gated by §6
Tracking notes bloat (modif history, verbose steps) and that hurts cold-start context elsewhere. Trim, but **only what already has a durable home** (§6) - never lose forward-looking content. **Surface the diff before applying.**
- **Resolved items** → one line + pointer (`✅ RÉSOLU <date> (commit/ADR) - <what>`); drop verbose `(description initiale…)` blocks.
- **De-dup** item-prose vs journal → one home (the item line carries the pointer, the journal carries the dated narrative; not both in full).
- **Journal** entries older than active relevance → condense or move to a `… Journal archive` note.
- **Target shape**: where the project fixes its own note structure (vault: `99-Templates/`), that structure wins - place each element in the whitelisted section that fits, add none. Elsewhere, top→bottom: frontmatter · 🔄 Reprise/Resume (jetable) · Statut/Status (1 line) · active priorities P0..P3 (value+trigger) · decisions (+ ADR refs) · resolved (one-liners + pointer) · journal (recent, terse) · debt.
Commit the compaction separately (distinct from §8).

## 10. Working-tree hygiene
Report uncommitted changes. Commit only in-scope files (project convention: per-group / per-task). Leave parallel-session files untouched.

## Rules
Terse. Reference SSoT/pointers, never restate values. **Persist (commit) before you trim.** Confirm before deleting or trimming anything. Surface every inference before writing.

Le plancher réel est déjà déclaré au bon endroit — `required_version = ">= 1.7.0"` dans `live/providers.tf` (1.1 moved, 1.5 import, 1.7 removed). Je supprime le fichier, on hérite de la racine.

**2. « Je ne vois pas le move »** : c'est le défaut de fond. `switch.sh` remplace les fichiers en silence, donc ni toi ni l'audience ne voyez **ce qui a changé**. Je lui fais afficher le diff.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Overlay a step snapshot into live/ - the state stays put, only the .tf files

set -euo pipefail

step="${1:?usage: switch.sh <step-1|step-2|step-3|step-4|step-5|step-5b|step-6>}"

cp "$src"/*.tf "$root/live/"

if command -v git >/dev/null; then
  git --no-pager diff --no-index --color=always -- "$before" "$root/live" 2>/dev/null \

else

fi

echo "next: cd live && terraform init && terraform plan"
EOF

Restauration faite, audit terminé. **Et j'ai trouvé le point décisif : Renovate.**

## Task 1 - le plan versions

**Les données** (pin `mise.toml` vs `required_version`) :

| Exemple | pin | plancher | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| check-health · check-conditional-policy | 1.5.0 | >= 1.5.0 | pile le plancher |
| secrets-out-of-state | 1.11.4 | >= 1.11.1 | +patch, **justifié en commentaire** (bug #36619) |
| aws-multi-env · actions · actions-lambda · query-import | 1.14.8/9 | >= 1.14 | pile le plancher |
| deferred-actions/02-after | 1.16.0-alpha | >= 1.16.0 | pile, gelé par Renovate |
| **aws-budget-cutoff** | **1.15.6** | **~> 1.9** | **6 minors au-dessus** |
| **module-testing** | **1.15.6** | **>= 1.9.0** | **6 minors au-dessus** |
| state-refactoring | (supprimé par moi) | >= 1.7.0 | à poser |

**Le point décisif** : `.github/renovate.json` bumpe **tous** les pins stables chaque semaine. Seuls les `-alpha|beta|rc` sont gelés. Les 2 « dérives » ne sont pas des erreurs d'auteur : Renovate les a fait monter. Donc la règle « pin = plancher » **se fait défaire toutes les semaines**, sauf à geler mise sous `examples/` — et alors plus rien ne teste tes exemples contre un Terraform récent.

**Ce que ça révèle : les deux valeurs répondent à deux questions différentes.**
- `required_version` = **le contrat**. « la version minimum où ce code marche ». Sémantique, ne dérive jamais, c'est *elle* qui illustre la feature.
- pin `mise.toml` = **la version testée**. Ce que toi et la CI avez réellement joué. Elle doit avancer, sinon une régression Terraform 1.16 passe inaperçue.

Sous cet angle, épingler mise au plancher est un piège : tu ne testerais plus jamais que la plus vieille version supportée.

**Ma reco - option A, mais avec la règle écrite** :
1. Racine garde `terraform` (version testée courante, bumpée par Renovate) + `tflint` + `trivy`.
2. Un exemple n'override **que s'il en a besoin**, et le commentaire dit pourquoi : alpha assumée (`deferred-actions`), version bloquée sur un bug connu (`secrets`), démonstration d'un comportement ancien.
3. Le **plancher vit en `required_version`**, jamais dans mise. C'est ce que lit un praticien.
4. Nettoyage : les overrides qui ne diffèrent plus de la racine sautent (budget-cutoff, module-testing, actions×2, query, multi-env, check×2 — à valider un par un).
5. Règle codifiée dans `AGENTS.md` §Toolchain, sinon elle redérive.

**Interaction à trancher avec toi** : `AGENTS.md` dit « tasks replace Makefiles » (`mise run <task>`). Si je te propose une tâche de démo (voir Task 2), elle a besoin d'un `mise.toml` dans l'exemple — même sans override de version. Ça peut militer pour ta piste B (un fichier partout). À arbitrer ensemble.

## Task 2 - switch.sh, et le coup de tournevis

**Ce qu'il fait aujourd'hui**, `./scripts/switch.sh step-2` :
1. copie les `.tf` actuels de `live/` dans un temp
2. affiche le **diff** temp → snapshot `step-2/`
3. remplace les `.tf` de `live/` par ceux de `step-2/`
4. **ne touche jamais** `live/terraform.tfstate` — c'est tout le principe : le state reste, le code change

**La friction que tu sens** : le script se lance depuis la racine de l'exemple, `terraform` depuis `live/`. Donc à l'antenne tu fais `cd ..` / `cd live` en boucle. C'est exactement le type d'hésitation qui t'a coûté 5 moments au S33.

**Trois options, ma reco en 3** :

| | Mécanique | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Deux terminaux : switch à gauche, terraform à droite | le diff et le plan sont sur deux écrans, l'audience perd le lien de cause à effet |
| 2 | Un terminal, `cd` à la main | ce que tu vis, ça hésite |
| 3 | **Une tâche `mise run step 2`** depuis n'importe où : affiche le diff → `init` si la source de module a changé → `plan`. Les commandes s'échoent avant de s'exécuter | un geste par palier, zéro `cd`, la chaîne diff → plan → « no changes » se lit d'un bloc |

En 3, tu gardes la main : le `apply` reste séparé, tu le tapes quand tu veux. Le script ne fait que ce qui est mécanique et répétitif.

Je code l'option 3 ? Et tu tranches A ou B sur les versions — j'applique dans la foulée.

**1. Versions : oui, c'est exactement ma reco.** Ta formulation la dit mieux que moi : le plancher est déjà dans le code (`required_version`), donc mise n'a pas à le redire. Mais en vérifiant : `switch.sh` résout sa racine depuis son propre chemin, donc **`../scripts/switch.sh step-2` marche depuis `live/`**. Tu ne quittes jamais `live/`, pas de `cd`, pas de tâche, pas de fichier. La remarque tombe.

**3. Ton objection sur le state est juste, et mon option 3 réglait le mauvais problème.**

Le vrai défaut n'est pas le nombre de terminaux. C'est que **code et state sont deux axes indépendants** :

- `switch.sh` déplace l'axe **code**
- `terraform apply` déplace l'axe **state**

Rien ne garantit qu'ils restent alignés. Si un palier casse à l'antenne, tu ne peux pas revenir : le code se rembobine, le state non. Et pour répéter ce soir, tu dois `destroy` + tout réappliquer à chaque tour.

**Ce que la structure du lab offre gratuitement, et que je n'ai pas exploité** : après le step-1, **aucun palier ne touche AWS**. Ce sont tous des mouvements de state (c'est la thèse du live : « un plan no changes »). Backend local ⇒ le state est un simple fichier.

**Le coup de tournevis, version corrigée** - trois verbes, un seul terminal, tu restes dans `live/` :

| Commande | Quand | Ce que ça fait |
|---|---|---|
| `../scripts/switch.sh save` | une fois, après l'apply du step-1 | snapshot du state dans `.baseline/` (gitignoré) |
| `../scripts/switch.sh step-N` | à chaque palier | diff des `.tf` + bascule, puis **affiche la commande exacte à taper** (`terraform plan`, ou `init && plan` s'il détecte un changement de source de module) |
| `../scripts/switch.sh reset` | répétition, ou incident à l'antenne | code → step-1, state → baseline, state d'`adjacent` supprimé. **Instantané, zéro appel AWS** |

Ce que ça débloque :
- **répéter ce soir** : la chaîne complète en boucle, chaque tour coûte une copie de fichier au lieu d'un `destroy` + réapply
- **filet à l'antenne** : un palier plante, `reset`, tu reprends — pas de trou de 4 minutes en direct
- **le geste reste le tien** : le script ne joue jamais `plan` ni `apply`, il prépare et il dit quoi taper

Cohérent parce que **après le step-1, aucun palier ne touche AWS** : tout est mouvement de state. C'est la thèse du live qui rend le rembobinage gratuit.

import io

new="""- **Root `mise.toml`** pins the toolchain for the whole repo: `tflint`, `trivy`, and the single `terraform` version every example is tested against. mise merges every `mise.toml` from the cwd up to the repo root, so an example inherits it by default.
- **The floor and the tested version are two different things - do not conflate them.** An example's minimum Terraform version is declared where a reader looks for it: `required_version` in its `.tf`, with a comment naming the feature that sets the floor. The `mise.toml` pin is the version CI and the author actually ran, and it moves forward (Renovate) so a regression in a newer Terraform is caught.
- **A per-example `mise.toml` overrides `terraform` only when the example cannot run on the root version** - e.g. an `experiment` that needs an alpha/rc. Pinning a floor there is a bug: it freezes the example on the oldest supported version and it is never tested against anything else. An example whose `mise.toml` holds only a redundant pin has no reason to exist; keep the file when it carries `[tasks]`."""
assert old in s
io.open(p,"w",encoding="utf-8").write(s.replace(old,new))
